name: Search for a Federal Corporation
description: Federal corporation search operated by Corporations Canada, confirming the existence of federally incorporated bodies.

publicAccess.notes: Record states: free to search. The overall access posture is not established, so the level stays unknown.

recommendedIndustries: Federally incorporated Canadian bodies
pros: Authoritative source for federal incorporation status
Free to search
cons: Excludes provincially incorporated companies and financial-law corporations
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. Provincial companies are covered elsewhere.

name: Canadian Patents Database
description: Canadian Patents Database is the federal patent register published by the Canadian Intellectual Property Office. It exposes Canadian patent applications and granted patents, with bibliographic data, claims and legal status, searchable without an account.

publicAccess.notes: The basic search form is reached directly with no account or sign-in step.

bestFor: Establishing whether a Canadian patent or application exists for a given invention or applicant.
Reading the bibliographic record and legal status of a Canadian patent without ordering a file copy.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming corporate existence, which the patent register does not record.
Treating an absent result as proof of novelty, because recent applications are not all publicly visible.
recommendedIndustries: Applicants and owners of Canadian patents
pros: The Canadian Patents Database can be searched free of charge and without an account, directly from the Canadian Intellectual Property Office.
The database records its own currency on the search page, which was stated as last updated 2026-08-05 when this record was verified.
It is the federal source of record for Canadian patent applications and grants rather than a commercial republication of them.
cons: CIPO states that patent applications filed less than 18 months ago are only available if the applicant specifically asks for them, so recent filings can be invisible.
CIPO warns that "due to the complexity of claims, vocabulary and different languages, it is practically impossible to find every relevant publication".
CIPO published a notice of irregularities in status information for certain applications and patents following its Next Generation Patents migration.
It records patents, not businesses, so it does not establish that an applicant is a registered entity.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official CIPO sources. Operator: Canadian Intellectual Property Office, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. The 18-month limitation and the search-completeness warning are quoted from CIPO’s "Search intellectual property databases" page. The status-irregularity notice was displayed on the search page at verification. Inclusion arises from a patent filing, not from any submission.

name: MRAS Canadian Business Registry
description: MRAS Canadian Business Registry is a federal search interface that queries participating provincial, territorial and federal corporate registers through the Multi-Jurisdictional Registry Access Service. It is a cross-registry lookup layer operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, not itself a register of record.

operator.name: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

publicAccess.notes: The interface is a client-rendered application whose search behaviour could not be exercised without running scripts, so the access posture is recorded as unknown rather than assumed.

bestFor: Locating which Canadian registry holds a corporation when the jurisdiction of incorporation is not known.
Moving from a federal starting point to the participating provincial register that actually holds the file.
notRecommendedFor: Use as the legal source of record, which remains the federal, provincial or territorial register the entity is filed in.
Establishing coverage across Canada, because only some provinces and territories participate.
recommendedIndustries: Corporations registered in participating Canadian jurisdictions
pros: It is operated by the Government of Canada rather than by a commercial aggregator, and canadasbusinessregistries.ca resolves to ised-isde.canada.ca.
It gives one federal entry point to corporate records that are otherwise split across separate provincial and territorial systems.
cons: It is a search interface over participating registers, not the legal source of record for any entity.
Coverage is limited to the jurisdictions that participate in the Multi-Jurisdictional Registry Access Service, so a Canadian corporation may be absent without being unregistered.
The interface renders through client-side scripts, so its search and access behaviour could not be established from the served page alone.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05. The public entry point https://canadasbusinessregistries.ca/ was confirmed by request to redirect to https://ised-isde.canada.ca/cbr-rec/en/, whose page title is "MRAS Canadian Business Registry". Classified as cross-border-registry-interface: it queries participating registers and is not the statutory register for any entity. The unrelated domain businessregistries.ca was checked and is a commercial domain-sale parking page with no government connection; it must not be cited as this service. Access fields stay null because the application is client-rendered and its behaviour was not exercised.

name: SEDAR+
description: SEDAR+ is the national filing and disclosure system of the Canadian Securities Administrators, carrying public securities filings by reporting issuers together with cease trade orders and disciplined lists. It is operated jointly by the provincial and territorial securities regulators rather than by a federal agency.

publicAccess.notes: The landing page was read directly; the filing-search interface returned an access error at verification, so no access behaviour is claimed.

bestFor: Reading the public securities filings a Canadian reporting issuer is required to make.
Checking whether an issuer or individual appears on a cease trade order or a disciplined list.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming corporate registration, which sits with the federal, provincial or territorial corporate registry.
Finding private Canadian companies, which are not reporting issuers and do not file there.
recommendedIndustries: Canadian reporting issuers and registered market participants
pros: It is the single national system through which Canadian reporting issuers make their required public disclosure.
It carries cease trade orders and disciplined lists alongside filings, which are the records a counterparty check most often needs.
It is operated by the provincial and territorial securities regulators themselves, so filings are held by the regulators rather than by an intermediary.
cons: It covers reporting issuers and market participants only, so the large majority of Canadian businesses never appear.
Filing fees are set by the provincial and territorial securities regulatory authorities, and the fee structure is not uniform across Canada.
The filing-search interface returned an access error when this record was verified, so its search behaviour is not established here.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the SEDAR+ landing page. Operator: the Canadian Securities Administrators, whose members include the British Columbia Securities Commission, the Alberta Securities Commission, the Ontario Securities Commission and the Autorité des marchés financiers, as named in the page footer. The landing page describes SEDAR+ as a system to "File, disclose and search for issuer information in Canada’s capital markets". The record search endpoint returned HTTP 403 at verification; access fields therefore stay null. Fees referenced are filing fees borne by filers, and no searcher fee is asserted here.

name: Ontario Business Registry
description: Ontario Business Registry is the provincial register of Ontario corporations, not-for-profit corporations and registered business names, operated by the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement. Basic entity information is searchable at no charge, while profile reports, certificates and document copies are priced products.

operator.name: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement

publicAccess.notes: Ontario states that anyone can search the registry free of charge for basic information; an Ontario Business Account is required only to file for your own business, not to search.

bestFor: Confirming that an Ontario corporation, not-for-profit or business name is on the provincial register.
Establishing basic entity status before deciding whether a priced profile report is worth ordering.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by Ontario.
Obtaining directors, officers or filing history at no cost, because those sit behind priced products.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in Ontario
pros: Ontario states that "Anyone can search the OBR for free to get basic information about a business or not-for-profit organization".
No account is needed to run a basic search, so a counterparty check costs nothing.
It is the single provincial register for Ontario corporations, not-for-profit corporations and registered business names.
cons: The free tier returns basic information only; a profile report is $8, a document copy is $3 and a certificate of status is $26.
It records Ontario registrations and does not establish federal incorporation.
Registrants must report changes within 15 days, so a record can lag a recent change by up to that period.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Ontario page. Operator: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement. Free-search wording, the $8 / $3 / $26 product prices and the 15-day reporting requirement are quoted from that page. Classified as a public-filing-database as well as a company-register because Ontario sells copies of documents filed with the registry as a $3 product, so filed documents are held and released, not merely indexed. The free search entry point is the ONBIS register item search on appmybizaccount.gov.on.ca. Inclusion arises from statutory registration, not from any submission.

name: Registraire des entreprises — Enterprise Register
description: The Quebec enterprise register is the provincial register of enterprises maintained by the Registraire des entreprises, recording enterprises that carry on business in Quebec together with the persons involved in their administration and operation. Québec publishes the register as public information and offers both a simple and an advanced search.

publicAccess.notes: Québec states the register is consulted free of charge and links the public to the Registraire’s own portal. The portal refused the request at verification, so the fee position is recorded from Québec’s statement and nothing further is claimed.

bestFor: Confirming that an enterprise carrying on business in Quebec is entered in the provincial register.
Identifying the persons recorded as involved in the administration and operation of a Quebec enterprise.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by Quebec.
Treating a register entry as a verification of the facts declared, which Québec places on the enterprise itself.
recommendedIndustries: Enterprises carrying on business in Quebec
pros: Québec states that the enterprise register can be consulted free of charge, so a counterparty check costs nothing.

The free consultation covers the Québec Enterprise Number, the registration status, the names used, the addresses of the institutions, the contact details of officers and directors, and the names of the ultimate beneficiaries.
Publishing ultimate beneficiaries at no charge puts Quebec ahead of most Canadian registers on beneficial-ownership transparency.
A natural person can be searched by name, which Québec describes as letting you know who you are dealing with.
cons: Québec states that service in English "is reserved for individuals covered by the exceptions stipulated in the Charter of the French language", so an English-language reader may not be entitled to the English interface.
The register portal refused the request when this record was verified, so no deep search path is published here and its login behaviour is not established.
It records Quebec registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the Gouvernement du Québec pages "Enterprise register" and "Find an Enterprise in the Enterprise Register" on quebec.ca, last updated by Québec on 2025-09-23. Operator: Registraire des entreprises. The free-of-charge wording, the list of freely consultable fields including "the names of the ultimate beneficiaries", and the Charter of the French language condition on English service are all Québec’s own. beneficial-ownership-register is recorded because Québec states ultimate beneficiaries are among the fields consultable free of charge. The search host registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca returned an access refusal citing excessive use at verification, so access fields stay null and searchUrl is null rather than guessed. English title "Enterprise register" is the Gouvernement du Québec’s own English rendering, not an editorial translation.

name: Régie du bâtiment du Québec — Licence Holders Register
description: The licence holders register of the Régie du bâtiment du Québec records contractors and owner-builders licensed to carry out construction work in Quebec. The Régie directs the public to the register to check a contractor or a licence number before engaging them.

publicAccess.notes: The Régie’s own site was read directly and points the public to the register; the register application itself was not exercised, so no access behaviour is claimed.

bestFor: Checking that a Quebec construction contractor holds a current Régie du bâtiment licence before engaging them.
Resolving a Quebec contractor licence number to the entity that holds it.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming that a contractor is an incorporated or registered enterprise, which is a corporate-registry question.
Assessing workmanship, which no licence register records.
recommendedIndustries: Construction contractors licensed in Quebec
pros: A Quebec construction licence is a statutory requirement, so the register describes a legal status rather than a voluntary listing.
The Régie du bâtiment du Québec directs the public to the register to verify a contractor or licence number, and publishes it itself.
The Régie separately publishes restricted, suspended and cancelled licences, so an adverse status is traceable.
cons: It covers construction licensing only and says nothing about a contractor’s corporate registration in Quebec.
The register application was not exercised when this record was verified, so its access and search behaviour is not established here.
The Régie publishes its site primarily in French, so an English-only reader may find the register harder to use.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Régie du bâtiment du Québec site. The Régie states "Pour rechercher un entrepreneur ou un numéro de licence, consultez le Registre des détenteurs de licence" and links "Vérifier la licence d’un entrepreneur" and "Licences restreintes, suspendues et annulées". English title "Licence holders register" is an editorial rendering of "Registre des détenteurs de licence" and is marked as such. Access fields stay null because the register application was not exercised. Distinct host from the Quebec enterprise register.

name: BC Registry Services
description: BC Registry Services administers the British Columbia registers of businesses, not-for-profit societies, cooperative associations and financial institutions, and states that the records it maintains are public records. Searches and certificates are supplied through its search unit and the BC OnLine service.

operator.name: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Citizens’ Services

publicAccess.notes: The Province’s description of the service was read directly; the registry application is client-rendered and was not exercised, so the access posture is recorded as unknown.

bestFor: Confirming that a British Columbia company, society or cooperative association is on the provincial register.
Obtaining a certificate of status or good standing for a British Columbia entity.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by British Columbia.
Expecting a free self-service search, because search products are supplied through the registry search unit and BC OnLine.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in British Columbia
pros: The Province states that registrations of businesses, societies and cooperatives are "maintained as public records".
It is the single provincial administrator for British Columbia companies, societies, cooperative associations and provincial financial institutions.
Certificates of status, certificates of good standing and certified copies of filed documents are available as defined products.
cons: Search and certificate products are supplied through the registry search unit and the BC OnLine service, and paid products exist.
The registry application is client-rendered, so its search and access behaviour could not be established from the served page alone.
The Province published service-level notices at verification, with names and search at five business days and other filings at ten.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the Province of British Columbia’s "BC Registry Services" page. The "maintained as public records" wording and the five/ten business-day service levels are the Province’s own, as published on 2026-03-20. Classified as a public-filing-database as well as a company-register because the Province lists "Copies of Filed and Registered Documents" and their certified variants as defined search products, so filed documents are held and released. The bcregistry.gov.bc.ca application returned no server-rendered content, so access fields stay null and searchUrl is null rather than guessed. OrgBook BC was examined separately and also renders client-side; it is recorded in the backlog rather than published.

name: Manitoba Companies Office
description: The Manitoba Companies Office maintains the provincial registers of corporations, business names, trade names and limited partnerships within the Consumer Protection Division. Manitoba states that the public may search the registry to establish who is behind a trade name and to obtain a list of officers and directors.

operator.name: Companies Office, Consumer Protection Division, Government of Manitoba

publicAccess.notes: The Companies Office description was read directly; the online service at companiesonline.gov.mb.ca presents a login portal and was not exercised, so no free-search behaviour is claimed.

bestFor: Establishing who is doing business behind a Manitoba trade name.
Confirming that a Manitoba corporation or limited partnership is on the provincial register.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by Manitoba.
Expecting the register to cover professional licensing, which the Companies Office does not administer.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in Manitoba
pros: Manitoba states that "The public may search the registry to obtain information (for example, who is doing business under the trade name, where the business is located, and to get a list of officers and directors)".
It is the single provincial office for Manitoba corporations, business names, trade names and limited partnerships.
It also administers Commissioner for Oaths and Notary Public appointments, so those statuses are traceable in the same place.
cons: The online service presents a login portal, and whether an anonymous free search exists was not established at verification.
It records Manitoba registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
The Companies Office publishes fees through a separate forms-and-fees section rather than on the main page.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Manitoba Companies Office site. Operator: Companies Office, Consumer Protection Division, Government of Manitoba. The public-search wording is Manitoba’s own. The transactional service at companiesonline.gov.mb.ca presents a sign-in form; because an anonymous search path was not exercised, freeToSearch stays null rather than being asserted either way. Inclusion arises from statutory registration, not from any submission.

name: Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies
description: The Registry of Joint Stock Companies is the Nova Scotia register of sole proprietorships, partnerships, companies, societies, co-operatives and business names. Nova Scotia publishes a search over the information those entities are required by law to file, including addresses, partners, directors and officers.

operator.name: Registry of Joint Stock Companies, Government of Nova Scotia

publicAccess.notes: Nova Scotia’s description of the search was read directly; the RJSC Connect application presented an interstitial challenge at verification and was not exercised.

bestFor: Confirming that a Nova Scotia company, society, co-operative or business name is registered.
Identifying the partners, directors and officers a Nova Scotia entity has filed.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by Nova Scotia.
Treating an entry as evidence of solvency or good conduct, which no registration record establishes.
recommendedIndustries: Entities registered in Nova Scotia
pros: Nova Scotia states the search covers information "required by law to be filed", including names and addresses, partners, directors and officers, and activity history.
One register covers sole proprietorships, partnerships, companies, societies, co-operatives and operating names.
Nova Scotia publishes the governing statutes alongside the register, including the Companies Act, the Societies Act and the Partnerships and Business Names Registration Act.
cons: Standard and certified copies of documents and reports are ordered as priced products.
The RJSC Connect application presented an interstitial challenge when this record was verified, so its access behaviour is not established here.
It records Nova Scotia registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Government of Nova Scotia pages for the Registry of Joint Stock Companies and its search. Classified as a public-filing-database as well as a company-register because Nova Scotia states the search covers "activity history, including filed documents and reports", and offers standard and certified copies of those filed documents. Governing statutes named by Nova Scotia include the Co-operative Associations Act, Community Interest Companies Act, Companies Act, Corporations Registration Act, Limited Partnerships Act, Partnerships and Business Names Registration Act, Private Investment Holding Companies Act and Societies Act. The transactional host rjsc.novascotia.ca returned an interstitial challenge; access fields therefore stay null and searchUrl is null rather than guessed.

name: Companies and Deeds Online
description: Companies and Deeds Online is the Newfoundland and Labrador registry service covering companies, co-operatives, condominiums, deeds, mechanics liens and lobbyists. It is published by the provincial government as a single online entry point to those separate registers.

publicAccess.notes: The service and its register sections were confirmed from the served pages; the company search itself returned a processing error at verification and was not completed.

bestFor: Confirming that a Newfoundland and Labrador company or co-operative is on the provincial register.
Reaching the provincial deeds, mechanics liens and lobbyist registers from one place.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by the province.
Relying on uninterrupted availability, because the service returned an error during verification.
recommendedIndustries: Entities registered in Newfoundland and Labrador
pros: It is published directly by the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador rather than by an intermediary.
One service covers companies, condominiums, co-operatives, deeds, mechanics liens and lobbyists.
The registry publishes a direct contact route for reporting problems, including a telephone number and a government email address.
cons: The service returned a processing error during verification, so its search behaviour and fee model are not established here.
The interface is dated and splits its registers across separate sections rather than offering one combined search.
It records provincial registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05. The served pages identify the service as "Companies and Deeds Online - CADO", Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, with sections for Companies, Condominiums, Co-operatives, Deeds, Mechanics Liens and Lobbyists. Direct requests to the company search returned the service’s own error page, so access fields stay null, searchUrl is null and no fee model is asserted. Re-verification of the search path is recorded in the backlog.

name: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry
description: The Saskatchewan Corporate Registry is the provincial register of business entities, delivered under agreement by Information Services Corporation rather than directly by a government office. The registry remains statutory while the service that fronts it is operated commercially and presents a sign-in wall.

publicAccess.notes: The Corporate Registry entry point presents a user name and password form together with a "Need an account?" path; no anonymous search was reachable from it at verification.

bestFor: Filing and maintaining Saskatchewan business information required by the province.
Establishing that Saskatchewan corporate records are held statutorily even though the service is delivered commercially.
notRecommendedFor: A quick anonymous counterparty check, because the entry point requires an account.
Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by Saskatchewan.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in Saskatchewan
pros: The registry is the statutory Saskatchewan corporate register, and the service states that information filed there is "required by the Government of Saskatchewan".
Submitted information is checked for completeness at the point of filing.
Saskatchewan participates in the Multi-Jurisdictional Registry Access Service, so its records are reachable from the federal cross-registry interface.
cons: The entry point requires a user name and password, so there is no anonymous public search from it.
The service is delivered by Information Services Corporation, a commercial operator, rather than directly by a government office.
Scheduled maintenance windows are announced on the sign-in page, so availability is not continuous.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05. The Corporate Registry entry point at corporateregistry.isc.ca is titled "ISC Customer Portal" and presents a sign-in form, an account-creation path and a maintenance notice; loginRequired is therefore recorded as true from direct observation. Operator type is "other" because Information Services Corporation is a commercial operator delivering a statutory registry, which is materially different from Alberta, where no government-operated public search exists at all. freeToSearch stays null: no anonymous search was reachable, so no fee model is asserted.

name: Northwest Territories Corporate Registries
description: Corporate Registries is the Northwest Territories register of territorial incorporations, extra-territorial registrations, societies, co-operative associations, partnerships and business names, administered by the territorial Department of Justice. Basic entity information is available at no charge through the Corporate Registries Online System.

operator.name: Department of Justice, Government of the Northwest Territories

publicAccess.notes: The territory states that basic information such as legal name, status and entity type is available free of charge, and that an account with a card on file is required only for a full entity profile.

bestFor: Confirming free of charge that a Northwest Territories entity exists and what its current status is.
Reaching scanned images of documents a Northwest Territories entity has filed.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by the territory.
Obtaining a full entity profile without paying, because that requires an account with a card on file.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in the Northwest Territories
pros: The territory states that "Basic information such as the legal name, status, and type of entity is available free of charge".
Entity profiles link to scanned images of the documents an organisation has filed, so the underlying record is reachable.
One register covers territorial incorporations, extra-territorial registrations, societies, co-operatives, partnerships and business names.
The territory publishes its certificate fees openly, at $20.00 for a certificate of compliance or good standing.
cons: A full entity profile requires an account with a valid Visa or Mastercard on file to pre-authorise funds.
It records territorial registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
Some of the published guidance documents are several years old, the oldest dating from 2015.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Government of the Northwest Territories Department of Justice pages for Corporate Registries and corporate registry searches. The free-of-charge wording, the card-on-file requirement for full profiles and the $20.00 certificate fee are the territory’s own. The search tool is named the Corporate Registries Online System. Inclusion arises from statutory registration, not from any submission.

name: Nunavut Legal Registries
description: The Legal Registries Division of the Nunavut Department of Justice administers the territory’s corporate registries together with its personal property registry, land titles office and securities office. Nunavut states that almost all records are available to the public to view or obtain copies.

operator.name: Legal Registries Division, Department of Justice, Government of Nunavut

publicAccess.notes: No online search interface was published on the division’s site at verification; the division directs enquiries to its office, so no online access behaviour is claimed.

bestFor: Identifying the office that holds Nunavut corporate, partnership and business-name records.
Establishing that Nunavut corporate records are public even where no online search is published.
notRecommendedFor: Self-service online verification, because the division published no online search interface at verification.
Confirming federal incorporation, which is recorded by Corporations Canada rather than by the territory.
recommendedIndustries: Entities incorporated or registered in Nunavut
pros: Nunavut states that "Almost all records are available to the public to view or obtain copies".
One division covers corporate registries, personal property, land titles and the securities office, so the holder of any Nunavut legal record is easy to identify.
The division publishes direct contact details for enquiries that its website cannot answer.
cons: No online public search interface for the corporate registry was published on the division’s site at verification, so verification means contacting the office.
The division published a notice that its website "is under construction" and that the public "should not rely on our website to reflect an up-to-date description of applicable securities law".
It records territorial registration and does not establish federal incorporation.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the official Nunavut Legal Registries site, operated by the Department of Justice, Government of Nunavut. The public-records wording and the under-construction notice are Nunavut’s own. No online corporate search endpoint was published; searchUrl is therefore null and access fields stay null rather than being recorded as restricted, which would assert a posture not evidenced. This is a genuine coverage limit of the territory, not a gap in research.

name: Canadian Trademarks Database
description: Canadian Trademarks Database is the federal trademark register published by the Canadian Intellectual Property Office. It carries applied-for and registered Canadian trademarks together with certification marks, distinguishing guises, geographical indications and plant breeders’ rights denominations, searchable by mark, owner, application or registration number and international registration number.

publicAccess.notes: The search form is served directly with no account, sign-in or landing barrier, with its search fields and the database’s own currency date visible on the page.

bestFor: Checking whether a brand name or logo is already applied for or registered as a Canadian trademark.
Establishing the owner of record, the filing date and the current CIPO status of a Canadian mark.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming that a company legally exists, which is a corporate-registry question and not a trademark one.
Clearing a mark on its own, because unregistered common-law rights arise in Canada and appear in no register.
recommendedIndustries: Owners and applicants of Canadian trademarks
pros: The Canadian Trademarks Database can be searched free of charge and without an account, directly from the Canadian Intellectual Property Office.
CIPO states the database "provides access to over 140 years of Canadian trademarks data" and that a searcher can "search and study more than 1.4 million Canadian trademarks".
Coverage includes "all active and inactive marks that were cancelled, expunged, abandoned or refused after 1979", so a lapsed mark stays traceable.
The database publishes its own currency on the search page, which read 2026-08-05 when this record was verified.
cons: It records trademarks, not businesses. An entry establishes nothing about whether the owner is an incorporated or registered entity, and nothing about its legitimacy or standing.
Unregistered common-law trademark rights exist in Canada and appear nowhere in the database, so a clear search is not a clearance opinion.
CIPO publishes a disclaimer about relying on the database and advises that searching intellectual property is complex enough to warrant a registered agent.
The Domain Rating shown is a dated measurement of the shared departmental domain ised-isde.canada.ca, not of this database.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official CIPO sources and revalidated immediately before publication: the search page at ised-isde.canada.ca/cipo/trademark-search/srch served its search form and reported "The database was last updated on: 2026-08-05". Operator: Canadian Intellectual Property Office, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. Coverage and volume quoted from CIPO’s "Introduction to the Canadian Trademarks Database", which also carries the disclaimer notice. The searchable categories — trademarks, certification marks, distinguishing guise, geographical indications and plant breeders’ rights denominations — were read off the search form itself. The advice to engage a registered agent is CIPO’s, from "Search intellectual property databases". This is a distinct statutory system from the federal corporation search: a different register, a different legal function, a different search URL and a different population of subjects. It shares the official host ised-isde.canada.ca with that record, so both declare the ised-isde-canada shared-host group and this record reuses the domain’s existing frozen Domain Rating snapshot verbatim — value 92, provider Ahrefs, measured 2026-08-04, status historicalSnapshot, measuredDomain ised-isde.canada.ca — read directly off ca-corporations-canada. No measurement was made, no API was called and no date was changed. The rating describes the departmental domain, not this database and not any individual page on it. Inclusion arises from a trademark filing, not from any submission.

name: CanadaBuys
description: CanadaBuys is the Government of Canada procurement service publishing federal tender notices, award notices and contract history. It is the single official point of access for doing business with the Government of Canada and the broader Canadian public sector.

publicAccess.notes: Tender notices, award notices, contract history and solicitation documents were all retrieved without an account. The service’s own account-access page uses the phrase "view and bid", but reading a notice requires no account; an account is used to bid and to receive notifications.

bestFor: Finding current Government of Canada tender opportunities and the contracts awarded from them.
Researching federal contract history, including which suppliers have been awarded past contracts.
notRecommendedFor: Checking whether a supplier exists, is registered or is in good standing, which is a corporate-registry question.
Reading a published notice as evidence that a supplier is eligible, approved or trustworthy.
recommendedIndustries: Suppliers to the Government of Canada and the broader Canadian public sector
pros: CanadaBuys can be searched free of charge and without an account, and solicitation documents are downloadable anonymously.
It publishes tender notices, award notices and contract history together, so a procurement can be followed past the opportunity stage.
It is published by Public Services and Procurement Canada as the official point of access rather than by a commercial aggregator.
Bulk procurement datasets are offered for download through the Government of Canada open data portal.
cons: It is a notice database, not a supplier register. Publication establishes nothing about a supplier’s eligibility, standing, competence or trustworthiness.
The account-access page is worded as though an account is needed to view opportunities, which understates what can be read anonymously.
Notice content is supplied by the contracting authority, so an error in a notice is the authority’s and is not corrected by the service.
The service intermittently refuses automated requests, so availability to a script is not a guide to availability in a browser.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official Government of Canada pages. Operator: Public Services and Procurement Canada. This record REVERSES a Wave 1C-2 rejection, and only on the classification question: CanadaBuys was previously rejected as "a tender-opportunity portal, not a register of businesses", which was correct under the type vocabulary then available. The public-procurement-notice-database type added in this wave describes it honestly, and the editorial standard is unchanged — it is still not a supplier register, and the record says so. Anonymous access was reproduced across notice, award, contract-history and solicitation-document retrieval; one earlier automated request returned an HTTP 403 interstitial, which is recorded as intermittent bot mitigation rather than a login requirement. Filed as scope national. domainRating stays null: canadabuys.canada.ca carries no existing frozen snapshot, so there is nothing to reuse and nothing may be measured.

name: FINTRAC Money Services Business Registry
description: The Money Services Business Registry is the searchable record of businesses registered with Canada’s financial intelligence unit before they may operate as money services businesses. The agency states that registration does not indicate endorsement or licensing, only that a business has satisfied the legal requirements to register.

operator.name: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada

publicAccess.notes: The registry page was retrieved directly and anonymously and documents its own behaviour — the agency states that all fields are searchable, that a downloadable version is available, and that the registry is updated monthly. No query was executed, so those are recorded as the operator’s documentation rather than as observed behaviour, every access boolean stays null and no search URL is published.

bestFor: Checking whether a money services business is currently registered in Canada, and verifying its registered name and number.
Distinguishing a registered business from one whose registration has been revoked, ceased or expired, which the registry records as separate statuses.
notRecommendedFor: Treating registration as approval. The agency states plainly that registration does not indicate that it endorses or licenses a business, and that it issues no licences or certificates of registration.
Obtaining information beyond the registry. The agency states it cannot provide further information about a business than what the registry makes available.
recommendedIndustries: Money services businesses operating in Canada
pros: Registration is a legal precondition to operating, so the registry is a genuine gate rather than a voluntary listing.
It distinguishes registered, revoked, ceased and expired statuses, so a reader can tell a current registration from a lapsed one.
The agency documents its own update cadence and states that a downloadable version is available, which makes the freshness of an answer checkable.
cons: Registration is not endorsement, licensing or approval. The agency says so directly, and says it issues no licences or certificates.
A registration status can lag reality: the agency notes that a business whose renewal is still being processed remains shown as registered past its expiry date.
No query was executed during verification, so the search behaviour is recorded from the agency’s own documentation rather than observed, and no search URL is published.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the agency’s own site rather than guessing a path, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The register-versus-guidance distinction the brief required was settled from the agency’s own navigation: the guidance landing page is a different page from the registry itself, and this record points at the registry. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The registration decisions of Canada’s financial intelligence unit under the proceeds of crime and terrorist financing legislation. The agency states that money services businesses must register before they begin to operate. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The registry is served from the agency’s own host; no external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The Money Services Business Registry page, alongside a separately published list of businesses whose registration has been revoked. What registration does NOT establish, in the agency’s own words carried into the published text: “Registration with FINTRAC does not indicate that FINTRAC endorses or licenses the business. It indicates only that the business has satisfied the legal requirements to register. FINTRAC does not issue licenses or certificates of registration to businesses it regulates.” The revoked-registration list is a separate page over the same registration data and is deliberately NOT published as a second record: it is a status view of one registry, not a distinct system. Registry types: financial-services-register for the regulated financial activity, and regulated-operator-register because the registered population is businesses authorised to operate in a supervised sector rather than individual practitioners.

name: List of Registered Telecommunications Providers
description: The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission’s list of organisations registered to offer telecommunications services in Canada. Registration is mandatory before an organisation may offer service and is free; it is a registration rather than a licence, and carrying traffic internationally requires a separate BITS licence.

publicAccess.notes: The list page was served anonymously with no credential and rendered its column headings — company name, contact name, email, phone, address and registration list — but no credential prompt was reached either way. The table body is loaded by JavaScript and displayed only "Loading..." to a non-executing client, so no entry was ever seen. Access level is therefore recorded as unknown and EVERY boolean stays null, including loginRequired: reaching a page anonymously is not the same as establishing that the register itself requires no credential. Identity and function were established from the Commission’s own describing pages, not from the application.

bestFor: Checking whether an organisation has registered with the Commission before offering telecommunications services in Canada.
Understanding the Canadian registration duty, which reaches local voice, VoIP, internet, long distance, wireless and payphone services.
notRecommendedFor: Treating registration as a licence. Registration is free and mandatory; carrying traffic internationally requires a separate BITS licence.
Relying on the entries as accurate or current. The Commission expressly disclaims responsibility for the accuracy, reliability and currency of the data.
recommendedIndustries: telecommunications
technology
pros: The registration duty is stated plainly by the Commission: an organisation must register before it can offer or provide customers with telecommunications services.
The stated scope is broad and explicit, covering local voice, Voice over IP, internet, long distance, wireless and payphone services.
Registration is free, so the list is not filtered by ability to pay a fee.
The Commission publishes a companion list of providers removed from the registration lists, with a reason, so a disappearance can be traced rather than merely noticed.
cons: This is a REGISTRATION, not a licence. The Commission grants nothing on registering, and an entry is not an authorisation to carry traffic internationally — that requires a separate BITS licence.

The Commission states that the information "has been provided by external sources" and that it "is not responsible for the accuracy, reliability or currency" of it, so an entry is a provider’s own submission rather than a verified fact.
Registration says nothing about technical quality, solvency, or compliance with obligations other than the duty to register, and it does not establish that a provider is currently offering service.
Absence does not establish that an organisation may not operate. Exemptions exist, and a provider removed from the list appears on the separate withdrawn-and-incomplete list rather than here.
The list is rendered by JavaScript and showed only a loading state to the client used for verification, so no entry, count or coverage was observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the Commission’s telecommunications section to its registration guidance and then to the list, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass in which all three quotations matched contiguous official text. The registration page states: "Before an organization can offer or provide customers with telecommunications services, it must register with the CRTC." and "All telecommunications providers that carry telecommunications traffic internationally must obtain a BITS licence." It also states "It’s free to register." The list page carries the disclaimer: "The information on these pages has been provided by external sources. The Commission is not responsible for the accuracy, reliability or currency of the information contained on these pages." FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The registration duty administered by the Commission; the register records the provider’s own submission. The Commission disclaims responsibility for its accuracy and currency. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: applications.crtc.gc.ca, the Commission’s applications portal, distinct from the crtc.gc.ca site that carries the describing pages. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public list at applications.crtc.gc.ca. The Commission’s root host served only a JavaScript shell to automated clients; the describing pages were reached through its English-language path. DUPLICATE AND BOUNDARY DECISIONS. The "Withdrawn and Incomplete Telecommunication Providers" list was NOT published as a separate record: it contains providers REMOVED from these registration lists and is the historical face of the same registration act, which the wave contract classifies as a current/historical toggle rather than a distinct statutory system. It is instead described in this record’s limitations, because a reader who finds nothing here needs to know where a removed provider goes. The Commission’s quality-of-service indicator list was REJECTED as a candidate: it reports operational performance, not an authorisation. The BITS licence is a genuinely distinct legal act and is NOT covered by this record, but no public register of BITS licensees was located — the Commission publishes BITS applications by year — so it is recorded as targeted research incomplete rather than published or merged.

name: YellowPages.ca
description: Canada’s principal commercial business directory, operated by Yellow Pages Digital & Media Solutions Limited. A free online listing is requested through the operator’s solutions site, and the same company’s terms define YellowPages.ca and its French counterpart PagesJaunes.ca as one set of sites.

operator.name: Yellow Pages Digital & Media Solutions Limited

bestFor: Canadian businesses wanting a listing in the country’s best-known commercial directory.
Businesses serving both English and French markets, since one operator runs both language properties under one set of terms.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses wanting to publish a profile directly. The free route is a request submitted to the operator, not self-service publication.
Anyone who needs the free tier’s exact contents documented in advance. The operator sets those out only after contact.
recommendedIndustries: local-services
retail
professional-services
pros: The operator is named unambiguously in its own terms: sites are “OWNED AND OPERATED BY YELLOW PAGES DIGITAL & MEDIA SOLUTIONS LIMITED”, and the same entity holds the YellowPages.ca and Canada411 trademarks.
A free listing route is documented on the operator’s own solutions site under the heading “REQUEST YOUR FREE ONLINE LISTING”.
Public business profiles are openly accessible, with no login required to view them.

Ratings appear on business profiles and the operator’s help section describes account holders being able to “give your opinion on your favourite businesses”, so a consumer review function is documented.
cons: The free listing is REQUESTED, not published. The operator’s wording is “REQUEST YOUR FREE ONLINE LISTING”, and what the free tier contains is not enumerated on that page.

Everything else the operator sells around the listing — priority placement, websites, search and social advertising, print — is a separate paid product, and none of it is evidence about the base listing.
Creating a listing is confirmed; claiming an existing third-party profile is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.
Whether verification is required, and by what method, is not documented, so nothing about verification is asserted.
Ratings and consumer opinions are documented, but whether a business can respond to them is not, and is not asserted.
The operator’s free-listing page carries a 2023 copyright line while the directory itself carries a current one, so the solutions site is less actively maintained than the directory.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s corporate terms of use, its solutions site and the directory itself, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “OWNED AND OPERATED BY YELLOW PAGES DIGITAL & MEDIA SOLUTIONS LIMITED”, “REQUEST YOUR FREE ONLINE LISTING” and the trademark attribution were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: Yellow Pages Digital & Media Solutions Limited, named in the corporate terms of use and in the trademark attribution on the free-listing page. LISTING CONTROL: The business requests a listing from the operator; self-service publication is not documented. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented. PUBLIC INTERFACE: yellowpages.ca, with public profiles under /business/ and the free-listing request at solutions.yp.ca/free-listing. DUPLICATE DECISION — PAGESJAUNES.CA ABSORBED: PagesJaunes.ca is NOT published as a separate record. The operator’s single terms of use defines “Sites” as “corporate.yp.ca, yp.ca, pj.ca, YellowPages.ca, PagesJaunes.ca, Canada411.com”, one company operates them all, and the directory itself offers direct language switching between the English and French surfaces. This is one product on two language surfaces, the same conclusion reached for Virgilio Aziende and PagineGialle. The surviving record is this one.  DUPLICATE DECISION — 411.CA NOT ABSORBED AND NOT PUBLISHED: 411.ca returned 502 in an earlier pass and responds normally now, so its earlier unavailability was transport failure, not absence. It names a DIFFERENT operator in its own footer (“© 411 Local Search Corp 2026”) and serves its own public profile URLs, so the duplicate tests are not met and calling it a duplicate would assert a shared listing identity nobody documented. But both of its business links — “Business solutions” and “Add your business” — route to solutions.yp.ca, so it exposes no listing action of its own and cannot be published on its own terms either. Recorded as an unresolved routing relationship for browser verification.  CANADA411 SEPARATE: Canada411.com is in the same trademark family but is a people-search product, not a business directory, and is out of scope rather than a duplicate.  NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, claim flow, free-tier contents, indexability, link attributes, traffic.

name: n49
description: A Canadian review-led business directory operated by N49 Interactive Inc. Its pricing page is unusually blunt about what the free tier is not: the operator lists the free listing as carrying no website link, no verification and no support, with all three sold as upgrades.
bestFor: Canadian businesses wanting a free listing on a platform that documents its tiers and prices openly.
Businesses that want to know exactly what a free directory tier withholds before deciding whether to pay.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses expecting a free listing to be verified or supported. The operator states the free tier is neither.
Anyone whose reason for listing is a link to their own website. The operator states the free tier does not include one.
recommendedIndustries: local-services
retail
professional-services
pros: The operator is named plainly in its own terms: “n49 is owned and operated by N49 Interactive Inc.”
The base listing is free and the terms say so twice over: “n49 does not charge members any fees for use of the site. n49 does not charge business owners to list their business on the site.”

The pricing page is exceptionally candid about the free tier’s limits, listing “No Website Link”, “Not Verified” and “No Support” as its own product description rather than leaving them to be discovered.
Paid tiers are priced openly, at $10.00 per month for a verified listing and $100.00 for a sponsored one, rather than being quoted only on request.
The terms recognise a distinct “Business Owner” role — someone who “has registered a business profile on the site” — so the creation route is defined in the binding document, not only in marketing.
cons: The free listing is explicitly NOT verified. The operator lists “Not Verified” as a characteristic of the free tier, and sells verification as a paid upgrade, so a free entry here carries no verification of any kind.

The free listing carries no link to your website. The operator states “No Website Link” for the free tier and lists a link only under the paid tiers. No link benefit is documented for a free listing and none is asserted.
The free tier also carries “No Support”, so there is no documented route to help if an entry is wrong.
Cost is not guaranteed to stay as it is. The terms reserve the right that “in the future, n49 may charge for any of the services and may change its fees from time to time in its sole discretion.”

Anything you post is licensed very broadly. The terms take “a non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid and royalty-free worldwide license (with a right of sublicense through unlimited levels and numbers of sublicenses)” over submitted content.
An account is required before a business profile can be registered, so this is not an anonymous submission.
Creating a profile is confirmed; claiming an existing third-party profile is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.

Reviews are central to the platform, but whether a business can respond to them is not documented and is not asserted. The AI review tool bundled with the most expensive tier is a separate product and establishes nothing about replying on the free one.
How the operator verifies a paid “Verified Listing” is not documented, so no verification method is recorded.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own terms of use and pricing page, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “n49 is owned and operated by N49 Interactive Inc.”, “n49 does not charge business owners to list their business on the site”, “No Website Link” and “Not Verified” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: N49 Interactive Inc., named in the platform’s own terms of use. LISTING CONTROL: The business registers an account and self-manages a business profile; a business dashboard is documented for paid tiers. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented. PUBLIC INTERFACE: n49.com, with the creation route at /add-biz and tiers set out at /pricing. COST DECISION: freemium, on the operator’s own explicit statement that it does not charge to list, combined with two documented paid tiers at stated prices.  VERIFICATION DECISION: verificationRequired is recorded as FALSE rather than unknown, because the operator states the free tier is “Not Verified” — an affirmative product statement, not an absence of documentation. The METHOD used for paid verified listings remains unrecorded because it is genuinely undocumented.  NOT ASSERTED: owner responses, claim flow, verification methods, indexability, link attributes, traffic. The paid tiers’ link-attribute wording is reported as the operator’s own product description and is NOT adopted by this record.
